headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Firecrawl’s broad egress plus Copilot’s repo/editor access can expose sensitive web/API-key content into vendor-hosted coding context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs, while GitHub Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers. If Firecrawl output is copied into Copilot Workspace or chat, attacker-controlled page text can be treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is pasted or synced into Copilot chat/Workspace buffers, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Copilot is asked to act on untrusted scraped text without provenance checks, malicious instructions can be followed.
mitigations: Paste only extracted fields, not raw pages.
Add a provenance banner to all Firecrawl outputs before handoff.
Require human review of any instructions found in scraped content.
Use a fixed schema for handoff between tools.
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys and has broad network egress; Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. If sensitive Firecrawl outputs are placed in editor buffers, Copilot can transmit them to a third party. That default path is dangerous and can leak secrets or proprietary data.
conditions: IF Firecrawl processes pages containing secrets or API keys and those results are opened in Copilot buffers, leakage is reachable.
IF Copilot Chat/Workspace is used on files containing Firecrawl outputs, those contents can be sent to GitHub-hosted services.
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs out of Copilot-visible files.
Redact secrets before opening results in the editor.
Use separate workspaces for scraping and coding.
Disable Copilot on files that may contain scraped sensitive data.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before editor sync.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl can make broad network requests and supports multiple instances; Copilot can write files and modify git state with per-editor shared state only. The pair can contend over the same repo or workspace if Firecrawl-generated artifacts are written into the project and Copilot edits them concurrently. No locking is documented, so overlapping writes are plausible.
conditions: IF Firecrawl writes generated artifacts into the same repository Copilot is editing, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
IF multiple instances of either agent operate on one workspace without locks, git or file-state races are reachable.
mitigations: Use separate output directories per agent.
Pause Copilot while Firecrawl writes artifacts.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Review diffs before accepting Workspace edits.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped content and structured data; Copilot’s Workspace/chat can turn that context into edits. If Copilot treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape or hallucinated extraction can cascade into incorrect code or repo changes. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the interaction exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as direct input to Copilot Workspace, unverified facts can propagate into edits.
IF Copilot is asked to implement changes from scraped instructions without cross-checking, cascading errors can occur.
mitigations: Verify scraped facts against the source page.
Require a second source before code changes.
Use Copilot only for drafting, not auto-application.
Annotate uncertain fields in Firecrawl output.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between scrape and edit steps.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while Copilot processes repo context and open buffers through GitHub-hosted services. If regulated or sensitive data from Firecrawl enters Copilot-visible files, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safest reading is a medium mismatch risk.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs contain regulated data and are opened in Copilot, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF the organization requires local-only handling for secrets, Copilot’s vendor-hosted context processing becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot-visible files.
Classify Firecrawl outputs before storage.
Use a separate compliant environment for sensitive scraping.
Review vendor terms for retention and residency.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for sensitive data.
